doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Family at her shows and bringing kin on stage
summary: Cousins enjoy hearing about Big Mama and Pa-Pa; she feels she brings family with her and connects with the room.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your parents or grandparents and cousins — have they had a chance to see you in your concerts?

Yeah a few have. Yeah. Down through the years I’ve had several of my cousins show up and they love it when I talk about our grandparents — Big Mama and Pa-Pa and growing up on the river. And once in a while I’ll mention their name — they get a kick out of that. And I feel like it’s a way to keep our kin folks alive, you know our kin folks very much in the music and for me it’s huge because it gives me a chance to, first of all, I get to bring them with me. I get to bring my Big Mama and my Pa-pa with me, and my mother, on stage with me. And then that goes back to your other question about I can open up and just let them sing through me. That’s really what you’re hearing on a lot of these concerts. They’re not concerts for me anymore. These are, you can call them concerts, but this has given me a chance, when I’m on stage I try to be true to myself and true to © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

the song, true to the energy in the room, and just be one with that. I could — it doesn’t even have anything to do with singing in English, which I’ve proven — many of us in the music industry when we sing anywhere where people don’t even speak English, it’s just something about making contact with what’s going on in the room, and that’s everything.
